text.p: Here are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA
- Four persons injured in explosion in Pristina, Kosovo province. Explosive device discovered and deactivated in Prizren.
- Belgrade students agree to return to classes on Friday but to resume strike on Monday if rector Dragutin Velickovic does not resign by that time.
- Serbia's private enterpreneurs threaten to go on general strike on March 26 demanding restoration of ministry for private enterprise and suppression of default interest on due taxes.
- Serbian government instructs university to restore normal situation or it will cut financing.
- Head of Democratic Centre Dragoljub Micunovic believes the climate is now favourable for dialogue on Kosovo and that Serbs and Albanians have politically matured.
- Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic will head the Serb delegation at the Brcko conference in Vienna on March 7.

- Decisive struggle at upcoming Serbian presidential elections will be between the candidate of the left and the opposition coalition Zajedno says head of the Serbian Renewal Movement Vuk Draskovic, one of the coalition partners.
- Director of Zastava trucks Jeftimir Cvetkovic rejects accusations of doubling truck producer FAP's production programme and says he supports healthy domestic competition.
- Announced privatisation of PTT Serbia will not go through before the end of year, says paper's source.
- New Democracy will decide by March 10 if it will run in coalition with the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) at the upcoming republican elections.
- Albania normalises trans-border traffic with Yugoslavia.
- From December 1996 to end of Febreuary 1997, 40,000 tonnes of imported wheat arrived at Novi Sad port and another 100,000 expected in March, says port director.
POLITIKA
- Serbian government resolves to fight crime and gray economy.
- Yugoslav government criticises Kosovo human rights report by U.N. human rights rapporteur Elisabeth Rehn.
- Yugoslav railways working with 40 percent capacity, machinery needs renewal and repairs, say officials.
- National Bank of Yugoslavia Board of governors decides to incorporate Slavija and JIK banks in Beobanka as means of their rehabilitation.
- Food and drink basket for four member family cost 2,214 dinars in February, which is 0.6 percent down on the previous months, according to official statistics.
- National Bank of Yugoslavia lowers discount rate to 2.5 percent from 4.5.
- Serbian government appoints its representatives in the University Council which excpected to hold constituent session shortly.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Electricity prices will not go up, says president of the Serbian power company EPS managing board Dragan Kostic.
- Independent Democratic Serb Party (SDSS) set up in Borovo Naselje, eastern Slavonia.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- What will pensions be like after January's reduction which will range between 12.8 and 30 percent. Due to new method of calculation, substantial growth of average monthly wages should not be expected, so at best pensions will stagnate, says pension fund expert Cveta Stamenkovic. -- Belgrade newsroom + 381 11 2224305
